[[:db/retract 17592186162610 :question/answer-fields 17592186160952] {:db/id 17592186161972 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-689613bd-55bf-5236-b19b-6e6b928e5d1e" "question-34033db1-99ab-5af1-b893-026e522543dd"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161764 :question/problem "Which of the following pairs $(x,y)$ are solutions of the Diophantine equation $3x+8y=5?$

- $(7,-2)$

- $(22,-8)$

- $(15,-5)$" :question/worked-solution "Let's check each pair in turn.

- $(7,-2)$ is a solution of our equation. Indeed, substituting $x=7$ and $y=-2,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+8y & =5 \\ 3\cdot 7+8\cdot (-2) & =5 \\ 21-16 & =5 \\ 5 & =5\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- $(22,-8)$ is *not* a solution of our equation. Substituting $x=22$ and $y=-8,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+8y & =5 \\ 3\cdot 22+8\cdot (-8) & =5 \\ 66-64 & =5 \\ 2 & \ne 5\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- $(15,-5)$ is a solution of our equation. Indeed, substituting $x=15$ and $y=-5,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+8y & =5 \\ 3\cdot 15+8\cdot (-5) & =5 \\ 45-40 & =5 \\ 5 & =5\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161973 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-ccf1e2c5-efff-5b3d-ba7c-30f178649720" "question-8955bc35-57b9-5c55-b8c0-47deb511cca7"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161765 :question/problem "Which of the following Diophantine equations have solutions?

- $18x+15y=24$

- $7x-28y=10$

- $9x+27y=16$" :question/worked-solution "Recall that a linear Diophantine equation

$$
ax+by=c
$$

has a solution if and only if $d \: | \: c,$ where $d = \text{gcd}(a,b).$  

With that in mind, let's examine each equation in turn.

- Equation I has solutions. We have $a=18,$ $b=15,$ and $c=24.$ Since

$$
d=\text{gcd}(18,15)=3
$$

and $3 \: | \: 24,$ our equation has solutions.

- Equation II has no solution. We have $a=7,$ $b=-28,$ and $c=10.$ Since

$$
d=\text{gcd}(7,-28)=7
$$

and $7 \!\not{|}\: 10,$ our equation has no solution.

- Equation III has no solution. We have $a=9,$ $b=27,$ and $c=16.$ Since

$$
d=\text{gcd}(9,27)=9
$$

and $9 \!\not{|}\: 16,$ our equation has no solution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161975 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-77383f6b-915f-5d79-b4cc-4a0aa033b4bc" "question-c669e825-e611-5b7c-b04d-1fdff3741695"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161767 :question/problem "Given that $(x,y)=(15,14)$ is a solution of the Diophantine equation $11x-13y=-17,$ and that $(\overset{\sim}{x},\overset{\sim}{y})$ is the solution with the smallest possible positive value of $x,$ what is the value of $\overset{\sim}{x}?$" :question/worked-solution "First, recall that a linear Diophantine equation

$$
ax+by=c
$$

has a solution if and only if $d \: | \: c,$ where $d = \text{gcd}(a,b).$  Moreover, if $(x_0,y_0)$ is a solution to the equation, then the general solution is given by

$$
\left(x_0+\dfrac{b}{d}t, \, y_0-\dfrac{a}{d}t\right), \qquad t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots
$$

Here, we have $a=11,$ $b=-13,$ $c=-17,$ and 

$$
d=\text{gcd}(11,-13)=1.
$$

 

Since $(15,14)$ is a solution of $11x-13y=-17,$ the general solution must be

$$
\left(15+\dfrac{(-13)}{1}t, \, 14-\dfrac{11}{1}t\right) = (15-13t, \, 14-11t),
$$

where $t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \, .$

The smallest possible positive value of $x=15-13t$ is attained when $t=1.$ Therefore, 

$$
\overset{\sim}{x} = 15-13 \cdot 1 = 2.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161974 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-385bffa1-c86b-563c-a6fa-f591b8055eb4"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161766 :question/problem "Consider the Diophantine equation $2x+7y=10.$ The integer pair $(\overset{\sim}{x},\overset{\sim}{y})$ is the solution with the smallest possible positive value of $x.$ What is the value of $\overset{\sim}{x}?$" :question/worked-solution "We have the linear Diophantine equation

$$
ax+by=c
$$

where $a=2,$ $b=7,$ and $c=10.$ We're given that the equation has solutions.

Notice that our equation can't be solved for either of the two variables using integer coefficients. So, let's find the linear representation of $\text{gcd}(2,7)$ using the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}7 & = & 2\cdot 3 & + & 1 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 2 & = & 1\cdot 2 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =7-2\cdot 3.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that $d=\text{gcd}(a,b) = 1$ and

$$
2 \cdot (-3) + 7 = 1.
$$

Multiplying this equation by $10,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot (-3)+7 & =1 \\ 2\cdot (-3)\cdot 10+7\cdot 10 & =10 \\ 2\cdot (-30)+7\cdot 10 & =10,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that $(x,y)=(-30,10)$ is a solution to our Diophantine equation.

Now, the general solution is

$$
\left(-30+\dfrac{b}{d}t, \, 10-\dfrac{a}{d}t\right) = (-30+7t, \, 10-2t),
$$

where $t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \,.$

The smallest possible positive value of $x=-30+7t$ is attained when $t=5.$ Therefore, 

$$
\overset{\sim}{x} = -30+7 \cdot 5 = 5.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-689613bd-55bf-5236-b19b-6e6b928e5d1e" :question/id #uuid "689613bd-55bf-5236-b19b-6e6b928e5d1e" :question/math-academy-id "q-93737" :question/problem "Which of the following pairs $(x,y)$ are solutions of the Diophantine equation $5x+6y=8?$

- $(-2,2)$
- $(-8,8)$
- $(4,-4)$" :question/worked-solution "Let's check each pair in turn.

- $(4,-4)$ is *not* a solution of our equation. Substituting $x=4$ and $y=-4,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+6y & =8 \\ 5\cdot (-2)+6\cdot 2 & =8 \\ -10+12 & =8 \\ 2 & \ne 8\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- $(-8,8)$ is a solution of our equation. Indeed, substituting $x=-8$ and $y=8,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+6y & =8 \\ 5\cdot (-8)+6\cdot 8 & =8 \\ -40+48 & =8 \\ 8 & =8\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- $(4,-4)$ is *not* a solution of our equation. Substituting $x=4$ and $y=-4,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+6y & =8 \\ 5\cdot 4+6\cdot (-4) & =8 \\ 20-24 & =8 \\ -4 & \ne 8\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-bf0b86e1-db82-5c78-85bb-75796ef36d8d"] :db/ensure $$

$$
({x}_{0}+\frac{b}{d}t,\,{y}_{0}-\frac{a}{d}t),\,t=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…
$$

$$
d=\text{gcd}(6,-4)=2.
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}8 & = & 6\cdot 1 & + & 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 6 & = & 2\cdot 3 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
2=8-6\cdot 1.
$$

As a result, we obtain that $d=\text{gcd}(a,b)=2$ and

$$
6\cdot (-1)+8=2.
$$

Multiplying this equation by $5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6\cdot (-1)+8 & =2 \\ 6\cdot (-1)\cdot 5+8\cdot 5 & =10 \\ 6\cdot (-5)+8\cdot 5 & =10,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that $(x,y)=(-5,5)$ is a solution to our Diophantine equation.

Now, the general solution is

$$
(-5+\frac{b}{d}t,\,5-\frac{a}{d}t)=(-5+4t,\,5-3t),
$$

where $t=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…\,.$

The greatest possible negative value of $x=-5+4t$ is attained when $t=1.$ Therefore, 

$$
\overset{∼}{x}=-5+4\cdot 1=-1.

have the linear Diophantine equation

$$
ax+by=c
$$

where $a=5,$ $b=9,$ and $c=8.$ We're given that the equation has solutions.

Notice that our equation can't be solved for either of the two variables using integer coefficients. So, let's find the linear representation of $\text{gcd}(5,9)$ using the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}9 & = & 5\cdot 1 & + & 4 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 5 & = & 4\cdot 1 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =9-5\cdot 1 \\ 1 & =5-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =5-4 \\  & =5-(9-5) \\  & =5\cdot 2+9\cdot (-1).\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that $d=\text{gcd}(a,b)=1$ and

$$
5\cdot 2+9\cdot (-1)=1.
$$

Multiplying this equation by $8,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot 2+9\cdot (-1) & =1 \\ 5\cdot 2\cdot 8+9\cdot (-1)\cdot 8 & =8 \\ 5\cdot 16+9\cdot (-8) & =8,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that $(x,y)=(16,-8)$ is a solution to our Diophantine equation.

Now, the general solution is

$$
(16+\frac{b}{d}t,\,-8-\frac{a}{d}t)=(16+9t,\,-8-5t),
$$

where $t=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…\,.$

The smallest possible positive value of $x=16+9t$ is attained when $t=-1.$ Therefore, 

$$
\overset{∼}{x}=16+9\cdot (-1)=7.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-689d977d-3444-59e0-820b-9f9df6194cc6"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-689d977d-3444-59e0-820b-9f9df6194cc6" :answer-field/id #uuid "689d977d-3444-59e0-820b-9f9df6194cc6" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-12d32afc-c2b4-50a2-814f-1fe63fd8b640" :answer-field/choices ["answer-2840c818-f52f-501c-b517-84262b345ec3" "answer-1fb7e86f-b6a2-5e65-a4e9-3e8866a4b4af" "answer-4c898dd7-d2e5-5bf5-bcbe-2fce1b2cb9f7" "answer-12d32afc-c2b4-50a2-814f-1fe63fd8b640" "answer-863b6321-f203-51e2-b989-9d423491553a"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2840c818-f52f-501c-b517-84262b345ec3" :answer/id #uuid "2840c818-f52f-501c-b517-84262b345ec3" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1fb7e86f-b6a2-5e65-a4e9-3e8866a4b4af" :answer/id #uuid "1fb7e86f-b6a2-5e65-a4e9-3e8866a4b4af" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "16" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4c898dd7-d2e5-5bf5-bcbe-2fce1b2cb9f7" :answer/id #uuid "4c898dd7-d2e5-5bf5-bcbe-2fce1b2cb9f7" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-12d32afc-c2b4-50a2-814f-1fe63fd8b640" :answer/id #uuid "12d32afc-c2b4-50a2-814f-1fe63fd8b640" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "7" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-863b6321-f203-51e2-b989-9d423491553a" :answer/id #uuid "863b6321-f203-51e2-b989-9d423491553a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "9" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186163216 :tutorial/content "A **linear Diophantine equation** with two variables $x$ and $y$ takes the form 

$$
ax+by=c,
$$

where $a,$ $b,$ and $c$ are integer constants. A **solution of a Diophantine equation** is any integer pair 

$$
(x,y)
$$

 that satisfies the equation.

For example, the Diophantine equation 

$$
2x+3y=9
$$

has an infinite number of integer solutions:

$$
(3, 1), \quad (6, -1), \quad (15, -7), \quad \ldots
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186163217 :tutorial/content "The linear Diophantine equation

$$
ax+by=c
$$

has a solution if and only if $d \: | \: c,$ where $d = \text{gcd}(a,b).$  

Let's use the theorem to test some Diophantine equations.

- Consider the equation

$$
2x+10y=17.
$$

Here, we have $a=2,$ $b=10,$ and $c=17.$ Notice that

$$
d=\text{gcd}(2,10)=2
$$

and $2 \!\not{|}\: 17.$ Therefore, according to the theorem, our equation has no solution.

Indeed, notice that the expression on the left-hand side ($2x+10y$) is always an even number, while the right-hand side of the equation ($17$) is an odd number. As a result, there is no solution. 

- Consider the equation

$$
4x+5y=7.
$$

Here, we have $a=4,$ $b=5,$ and $c=7.$ Since 

$$
d=\text{gcd}(4,5)=1
$$

and $1 \:{|}\: 7,$ our equation has solutions.

Indeed, one of the solutions for $4x+5y=7$ is the pair $(3,-1).$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186163218 :tutorial/content "If $(x_0,y_0)$ is any particular solution of the equation, then the set of all solutions consists of integer pairs  

$$
\left( x_0 + \dfrac{b}{d}t, \: y_0 - \dfrac{a}{d}t \right), \qquad t = 0, \pm 1, \pm2, \ldots \: .
$$

In particular, if $d=1,$ we obtain

$$
\left( x_0 + bt, \: y_0 - at \right), \qquad t = 0, \pm 1, \pm2, \ldots \: .
$$

For example, given that $(x,y)=(4,-1)$ is a solution of the Diophantine equation 

$$
4x+5y=11,
$$

find its general solution. 

Here, we have $a=4,$ $b=5,$ and $c=11.$ Since $(4,-1)$ is a solution of $4x+5y=11,$ the general solution must be

$$
\begin{aligned}(4+\frac{5}{1}t,\,-1-\frac{4}{1}t) & =(4+5t,\,-1-4t),\end{aligned}
$$

where $t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \, .$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186162209 :activity/expected-seconds 960.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

$$

$$

- Equation II has no solution. We have $a=7,$ $b=-28,$ and $c=10.$ Since

$$

and $7 \!\not{|}\: 10,$ our equation has no solution.

- Equation III has no solution. We have $a=9,$ $b=27,$ and $c=16.$ Since

$$

$$

and $9 \!\not{|}\: 16,$ our equation has no solution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161975 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-77383f6b-915f-5d79-b4cc-4a0aa033b4bc" "question-c669e825-e611-5b7c-b04d-1fdff3741695"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161767 :question/problem "Given that $(x,y)=(15,14)$ is a solution of the Diophantine equation $11x-13y=-17,$ and that $(\overset{\sim}{x},\overset{\sim}{y})$ is the solution with the smallest possible positive value of $x,$ what is the value of $\overset{\sim}{x}?$" :question/worked-solution "First, recall that a linear Diophantine equation

$$
ax+by=c
$$

has a solution if and only if $d \: | \: c,$ where $d = \text{gcd}(a,b).$  Moreover, if $(x_0,y_0)$ is a solution to the equation, then the general solution is given by

where $t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \, .$

The smallest possible positive value of $x=15-13t$ is attained when $t=1.$ Therefore, 

$$
\overset{\sim}{x} = 15-13 \cdot 1 = 2.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161974 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-385bffa1-c86b-563c-a6fa-f591b8055eb4"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161766 :question/problem "Consider the Diophantine equation $2x+7y=10.$ The integer pair $(\overset{\sim}{x},\overset{\sim}{y})$ is the solution with the smallest possible positive value of $x.$ What is the value of $\overset{\sim}{x}?$" :question/worked-solution "We have the linear Diophantine equation

Notice that our equation can't be solved for either of the two variables using integer coefficients. So, let's find the linear representation of $\text{gcd}(2,7)$ using the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =7-2\cdot 3.\end{aligned}

$$

which means that $(x,y)=(-30,10)$ is a solution to our Diophantine equation.

Now, the general solution is

$$
\left(-30+\dfrac{b}{d}t, \, 10-\dfrac{a}{d}t\right) = (-30+7t, \, 10-2t),
$$

where $t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \,.$

The smallest possible positive value of $x=-30+7t$ is attained when $t=5.$ Therefore, 

$$
\overset{\sim}{x} = -30+7 \cdot 5 = 5.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-689613bd-55bf-5236-b19b-6e6b928e5d1e" :question/id #uuid "689613bd-55bf-5236-b19b-6e6b928e5d1e" :question/math-academy-id "q-93737" :question/problem "Which of the following pairs $(x,y)$ are solutions of the Diophantine equation $5x+6y=8?$

:question/problem "Which of the following pairs $(x,y)$ are solutions of the Diophantine equation $2x+5y=200?$

- $(15,35)$" :question/worked-solution "Let's check each pair in turn.

- $(20,32)$ is a solution of our equation. Indeed, substituting $x=20$ and $y=32,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+5y & =200 \\ 2\cdot 20+5\cdot 32 & =200 \\ 40+160 & =200 \\ 200 & =200\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- $(10,20)$ is *not* a solution of our equation. Substituting $x=10$ and $y=20,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+5y & =200 \\ 2\cdot 10+5\cdot 20 & =200 \\ 20+100 & =200 \\ 120 & \ne 200\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- $(15,35)$ is *not* a solution of our equation. Substituting $x=15$ and $y=35,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+5y & =200 \\ 2\cdot 15+5\cdot 35 & =200 \\ 30+175 & =200 \\ 205 & \ne 200\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-27a54542-1615-5cf2-b688-855028ab2529"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-27a54542-1615-5cf2-b688-855028ab2529" :answer-field/id #uuid "27a54542-1615-5cf2-b688-855028ab2529" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-65247087-2b2c-5c14-9dbe-ed7ca6e9451b" :answer-field/choices ["answer-2eb51416-f701-5ee9-b8ba-890cb4fc290c" "answer-41acb45f-a093-5fc2-ab40-01131398008b" "answer-65247087-2b2c-5c14-9dbe-ed7ca6e9451b" "answer-e43f6e8e-2053-5481-a5ab-80957e4905bf" "answer-87ed7622-25d5-5050-a518-3bf70496d27a"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2eb51416-f701-5ee9-b8ba-890cb4fc290c" :answer/id #uuid "2eb51416-f701-5ee9-b8ba-890cb4fc290c" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "I and II only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-41acb45f-a093-5fc2-ab40-01131398008b" :answer/id #uuid "41acb45f-a093-5fc2-ab40-01131398008b" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "I and III only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-65247087-2b2c-5c14-9dbe-ed7ca6e9451b" :answer/id #uuid "65247087-2b2c-5c14-9dbe-ed7ca6e9451b" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "I only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e43f6e8e-2053-5481-a5ab-80957e4905bf" :answer/id #uuid "e43f6e8e-2053-5481-a5ab-80957e4905bf" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "II only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-87ed7622-25d5-5050-a518-3bf70496d27a" :answer/id #uuid "87ed7622-25d5-5050-a518-3bf70496d27a" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "III only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-ccf1e2c5-efff-5b3d-ba7c-30f178649720" :question/id #uuid "ccf1e2c5-efff-5b3d-ba7c-30f178649720" :question/math-academy-id "q-93795" :question/problem "Which of the following Diophantine equations have solutions?

d=\text{gcd}(-3,-9)=3

- Equation III has solutions. We have $a=-12,$ $b=15,$ and $c=21.$ Since

$$

and $3\,|\,21,$ our equation has solutions.

have the linear Diophantine equation

$$
ax+by=c
$$

where $a=5,$ $b=9,$ and $c=8.$ We're given that the equation has solutions.

Notice that our equation can't be solved for either of the two variables using integer coefficients. So, let's find the linear representation of $\text{gcd}(5,9)$ using the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}9 & = & 5\cdot 1 & + & 4 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 5 & = & 4\cdot 1 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =9-5\cdot 1 \\ 1 & =5-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =5-4 \\  & =5-(9-5) \\  & =5\cdot 2+9\cdot (-1).\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that $d=\text{gcd}(a,b)=1$ and

$$
5\cdot 2+9\cdot (-1)=1.
$$

Multiplying this equation by $8,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot 2+9\cdot (-1) & =1 \\ 5\cdot 2\cdot 8+9\cdot (-1)\cdot 8 & =8 \\ 5\cdot 16+9\cdot (-8) & =8,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that $(x,y)=(16,-8)$ is a solution to our Diophantine equation.

Now, the general solution is

$$
(16+\frac{b}{d}t,\,-8-\frac{a}{d}t)=(16+9t,\,-8-5t),
$$

where $t=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…\,.$

The smallest possible positive value of $x=16+9t$ is attained when $t=-1.$ Therefore, 

$$
\overset{∼}{x}=16+9\cdot (-1)=7.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-689d977d-3444-59e0-820b-9f9df6194cc6"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-689d977d-3444-59e0-820b-9f9df6194cc6" :answer-field/id #uuid "689d977d-3444-59e0-820b-9f9df6194cc6" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-12d32afc-c2b4-50a2-814f-1fe63fd8b640" :answer-field/choices ["answer-2840c818-f52f-501c-b517-84262b345ec3" "answer-1fb7e86f-b6a2-5e65-a4e9-3e8866a4b4af" "answer-4c898dd7-d2e5-5bf5-bcbe-2fce1b2cb9f7" "answer-12d32afc-c2b4-50a2-814f-1fe63fd8b640" "answer-863b6321-f203-51e2-b989-9d423491553a"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2840c818-f52f-501c-b517-84262b345ec3" :answer/id #uuid "2840c818-f52f-501c-b517-84262b345ec3" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1fb7e86f-b6a2-5e65-a4e9-3e8866a4b4af" :answer/id #uuid "1fb7e86f-b6a2-5e65-a4e9-3e8866a4b4af" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "16" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4c898dd7-d2e5-5bf5-bcbe-2fce1b2cb9f7" :answer/id #uuid "4c898dd7-d2e5-5bf5-bcbe-2fce1b2cb9f7" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-12d32afc-c2b4-50a2-814f-1fe63fd8b640" :answer/id #uuid "12d32afc-c2b4-50a2-814f-1fe63fd8b640" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "7" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-863b6321-f203-51e2-b989-9d423491553a" :answer/id #uuid "863b6321-f203-51e2-b989-9d423491553a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "9" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186163216 :tutorial/content "A **linear Diophantine equation** with two variables $x$ and $y$ takes the form 

$$
ax+by=c,
$$

where $a,$ $b,$ and $c$ are integer constants. A **solution of a Diophantine equation** is any integer pair 

$$
(x,y)
$$

 that satisfies the equation.

For example, the Diophantine equation 

$$
2x+3y=9
$$

has an infinite number of integer solutions:

$$
(3, 1), \quad (6, -1), \quad (15, -7), \quad \ldots
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186163217 :tutorial/content "The linear Diophantine equation

$$
ax+by=c
$$

has a solution if and only if $d \: | \: c,$ where $d = \text{gcd}(a,b).$  

Let's use the theorem to test some Diophantine equations.

- Consider the equation

$$
2x+10y=17.
$$

Here, we have $a=2,$ $b=10,$ and $c=17.$ Notice that

$$
d=\text{gcd}(2,10)=2
$$

and $2 \!\not{|}\: 17.$ Therefore, according to the theorem, our equation has no solution.

Indeed, notice that the expression on the left-hand side ($2x+10y$) is always an even number, while the right-hand side of the equation ($17$) is an odd number. As a result, there is no solution. 

- Consider the equation

$$
4x+5y=7.
$$

Here, we have $a=4,$ $b=5,$ and $c=7.$ Since 

$$
d=\text{gcd}(4,5)=1
$$

and $1 \:{|}\: 7,$ our equation has solutions.

Indeed, one of the solutions for $4x+5y=7$ is the pair $(3,-1).$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186163218 :tutorial/content "If $(x_0,y_0)$ is any particular solution of the equation, then the set of all solutions consists of integer pairs  

$$
\left( x_0 + \dfrac{b}{d}t, \: y_0 - \dfrac{a}{d}t \right), \qquad t = 0, \pm 1, \pm2, \ldots \: .
$$

In particular, if $d=1,$ we obtain

$$
\left( x_0 + bt, \: y_0 - at \right), \qquad t = 0, \pm 1, \pm2, \ldots \: .
$$

For example, given that $(x,y)=(4,-1)$ is a solution of the Diophantine equation 

$$
4x+5y=11,
$$

find its general solution. 

Here, we have $a=4,$ $b=5,$ and $c=11.$ Since $(4,-1)$ is a solution of $4x+5y=11,$ the general solution must be

$$

where $t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \, .$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186162209 :activity/expected-seconds 960.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}] "assertions" [[17592186161764 :question/problem "Which of the following pairs $(x,y)$ are solutions of the Diophantine equation $3x+8y=5?$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only.""] [17592186161767 :question/problem "Given that $(x,y)=(15,14)$ is a solution of the Diophantine equation $11x-13y=-17,$ and that $(\overset{\sim}{x},\overset{\sim}{y})$ is the solution with the smallest possible positive value of $x,$ what is the value of $\overset{\sim}{x}?$"] [17592186161767 :question/worked-solution "First, recall that a linear Diophantine equation

$$
ax+by=c
$$

has a solution if and only if $d \: \mid \: c$, where

$$
d = \text{gcd}(a,b)
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each equation in turn.

- Equation I has solutions. We have $a=18$, $b=15$, and $c=24$. Since
$d=\text{gcd}(18,15)=3$
and $3 \: \mid \: 24$, our equation has solutions.
- Equation II has no solution. We have $a=7$, $b=-28$, and $c=10$. Since
$d=\text{gcd}(7,-28)=7$
and $7 \!\not{\mid}\: 10$, our equation has no solution.
- Equation III has no solution. We have $a=9$, $b=27$, and $c=16$. Since
$d=\text{gcd}(9,27)=9$
and $9 \!\not{\mid}\: 16$, our equation has no solution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only.""} {:db/id 17592186049540} {:db/id 17592186162577 :question/id #uuid "02d30137-346f-5a41-bf81-78c06fcb3090" :question/math-academy-id "q-92276"} {:db/id 17592186162605 :question/id #uuid "4701657e-f1b3-5a6c-805e-08bfdffec97f" :question/math-academy-id "q-93800"} {:db/id 17592186161974 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186161766 :question/id #uuid "5771c3fd-b47b-5f51-bc0c-d87771df70d7" :question/math-academy-id "e-8136"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "b68b2579-6ae9-53a4-a9f1-b36ff041d500" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186049094}] :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186162578 :question/id #uuid "6ac52016-11c7-524c-b2f3-76a9df291116" :question/math-academy-id "q-92562"} {:db/id 17592186162610 :question/id #uuid "111dc48c-89a1-58b9-b26b-03172f489d0e" :question/math-academy-id "q-93880"} {:db/id 17592186378004 :question/id #uuid "07071c90-36c9-5e91-95a8-b12580d541fd" :question/math-academy-id "q-93883"} {:db/id 17592186378011 :question/id #uuid "e6daeb0c-4af1-5a7b-8f44-73ef5ee456eb" :question/math-academy-id "q-93884"}] :knowledge-point/title "Solving a Linear Diophantine Equation"} {:db/id 17592186161766 :question/id #uuid "5771c3fd-b47b-5f51-bc0c-d87771df70d7" :question/math-academy-id "e-8136" :knowledge-point/_canonical-example [{:db/id 17592186161974 :knowledge-point/id #uuid "b68b2579-6ae9-53a4-a9f1-b36ff041d500" :knowledge-point/title "Solving a Linear Diophantine Equation"}] :question/problem "Consider the Diophantine equation $2x+7y=10$. What is the value of $\overset{\sim}{x}$?" :question/worked-solution "We have the linear Diophantine equation

$$
ax+by=c
$$

where $a=2$, $b=7$, and $c=10$. We're given that the equation has solutions.

Notice that our equation can't be solved for either of the two variables using integer coefficients. So, let's find the linear representation of $\text{gcd}(2,7)$ using the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}
7 &= \begin{vmatrix}2 \cdot 3 & +\end{vmatrix}1 \\
↙\begin{vmatrix}↙ \\ 2 &= \end{vmatrix}1 \cdot 2 \mid + \mid 0
\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}
1 &= 7 - 2 \cdot 3
\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that

$$
d=\text{gcd}(a,b) = 1
$$

and

$$
2 \cdot (-3) + 7 = 1
$$

Multiplying this equation by $10$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}
2 \cdot (-3) + 7 &= 1 \\
2 \cdot (-3) \cdot 10 + 7 \cdot 10 &= 10 \\
2 \cdot (-30) + 7 \cdot 10 &= 10
\end{aligned}
$$

which means that

$$
(x,y)=(-30,10)
$$

is a solution to our Diophantine equation.

Now, the general solution is

$$
\left(-30+\dfrac{b}{d}t, \, 10-\dfrac{a}{d}t\right) = (-30+7t, \, 10-2t)
$$

where

$$
t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \,
$$

The smallest possible positive value of

$$
x=-30+7t
$$

is attained when $t=5$. Therefore,

$$
\overset{\sim}{x} = -30+7 \cdot 5 = 5
$$"} {:db/id 17592186049094} {:db/id 17592186162578 :question/id #uuid "6ac52016-11c7-524c-b2f3-76a9df291116" :question/math-academy-id "q-92562"} {:db/id 17592186162610 :question/id #uuid "111dc48c-89a1-58b9-b26b-03172f489d0e" :question/math-academy-id "q-93880" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186161974 :knowledge-point/id #uuid "b68b2579-6ae9-53a4-a9f1-b36ff041d500" :knowledge-point/title "Solving a Linear Diophantine Equation"}] :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "99045d38-a490-54c0-b373-341855fc30c3" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "-3" :db/id 17592186160953} {:answer/id #uuid "d600bb19-1ac6-5aee-a07a-3a01a7701761" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "-1" :db/id 17592186160954} {:answer/id #uuid "0a212525-4cf7-5285-bd4c-14473712ced4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "-2" :db/id 17592186160955} {:answer/id #uuid "51302934-3c74-5cb2-9eb7-891902b6daf3" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "-4" :db/id 17592186160956} {:answer/id #uuid "61bbb7c1-cd0b-5060-ab1c-bba28d16b30a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "-5" :db/id 17592186160957}] :answer-field/id #uuid "fd7111de-7240-5214-91ff-4e944eb7cfac" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493 :db/ident :answer-field.type/radio} :db/id 17592186160952}] :question/problem "Consider the Diophantine equation $6x + 8y = 10$. $$

$$
d = \text{gcd}(a,b)
$$

Moreover, if $(x_0,y_0)$ is a solution to the equation, then the general solution is given by

$$
\left(x_0+\dfrac{b}{d}t, \, y_0-\dfrac{a}{d}t\right), \qquad t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots
$$

Here, we have $a=11$, $b=-13$, $c=-17$, and

$$
d=\text{gcd}(11,-13)=1
$$

Since $(15,14)$ is a solution of

$$
11x-13y=-17
$$

the general solution must be

$$
\left(15+\dfrac{(-13)}{1}t, \, 14-\dfrac{11}{1}t\right) = (15-13t, \, 14-11t)
$$

where

$$
t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \,
$$

The smallest possible positive value of $x=15-13t$ is attained when $t=1$. Therefore,

$$
\overset{\sim}{x} = 15-13 \cdot 1 = 2
$$"} {:db/id 17592186162579 :question/id #uuid "df62334c-3c61-58f7-8140-cdb1537eea8a" :question/math-academy-id "q-92564"} {:db/id 17592186162580 :question/id #uuid with two variables $x$ and $y$ takes the form

$$
ax+by=c
$$

where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are integer constants. A **solution of a Diophantine equation** is any integer pair $(x,y)$ that satisfies the equation.

For example, the Diophantine equation

$$
2x+3y=9
$$

has an infinite number of integer solutions:

$$
(3, 1), \quad (6, -1), \quad (15, -7), \quad \ldots
$$" :tutorial/id #uuid "74479694-00cd-56e4-a966-17ec3c6a6df4" :tutorial/math-academy-id 4859 :tutorial/title "Introduction"} :step/id #uuid "8fdb2ed6-395d-5acd-a018-d4c94702acd2" :step/math-academy-id 30433 :step/next {:db/id 17592186162835}} {:db/id 17592186162835 :step/content {:db/id 17592186161972 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186161764 :question/id #uuid "41efb6ec-beb7-52ff-9951-fd73454e50d6" :question/math-academy-id "e-8134"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "8919d471-0e4c-55c1-b39e-2b46a86540d2" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186048714}] :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186162576} {:db/id 17592186162604}] :knowledge-point/title "Identifying a Solution of a Linear Diophantine Equation"} :step/id #uuid "a32eefb7-ec52-5fbb-a2ee-f1bfe513b195" :step/math-academy-id 30434 :step/next {:db/id 17592186162837}} {:db/id 17592186162836 :step/content {:db/id 17592186161973 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186161765 :question/id #uuid "b156d26b-369f-57d7-8fcf-3e67f2c03e60" :question/math-academy-id "e-8135"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "607df418-165b-5d37-aae1-d49ce8e9d3e5" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186049540}] :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186162577} {:db/id 17592186162605}] :knowledge-point/title "Identifying Whether a Linear Diophantine Equation Has a Solution"} :step/id #uuid "4452042f-220b-53ea-a8da-dfb2eabdd9ed" :step/math-academy-id 30435 :step/next {:db/id 17592186162839}} {:db/id 17592186162837 :step/content {:db/id 17592186163217 :tutorial/content "The linear Diophantine equation

$$
ax+by=c
$$

has a solution if and only if $d \: \mid \: c$, where

$$
d = \text{gcd}(a,b)
$$

Let's use the theorem to test some Diophantine equations.

- Consider the equation
$2x+10y=17$.
Here, we have $a=2$, $b=10$, and $c=17$. Notice that
$d=\text{gcd}(2,10)=2$
and $2 \!\not{\mid}\: 17$. Therefore, according to the theorem, our equation has no solution.

Indeed, notice that the expression on the left-hand side ($2x+10y$) is always an even number, while the right-hand side of the equation ($17$) is an odd number. As a result, there is no solution.

- Consider the equation
$4x+5y=7$.
Here, we have $a=4$, $b=5$, and $c=7$. Since
$d=\text{gcd}(4,5)=1$
and $1 \:{\mid}\: 7$, our equation has solutions.

Indeed, one of the solutions for

$$
4x+5y=7
$$

is the pair $(3,-1)$." :tutorial/id #uuid "a6d53d84-2ce8-5b31-b71b-49fa570f368e" :tutorial/math-academy-id 4860 :tutorial/title "When a Linear Diophantine Equation Has No Solutions"} :step/id #uuid "bdfa6024-4717-5bbc-92b3-98318be5fc5f" :step/math-academy-id 30436 :step/next {:db/id 17592186162836}} {:db/id 17592186162838 :step/content {:db/id 17592186161974 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186161766 :question/id #uuid "5771c3fd-b47b-5f51-bc0c-d87771df70d7" :question/math-academy-id "e-8136"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "b68b2579-6ae9-53a4-a9f1-b36ff041d500" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186049094}] :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186162578} {:db/id 17592186162610} {:db/id 17592186378004} {:db/id 17592186378011}] :knowledge-point/title "Solving a Linear Diophantine Equation"} :step/id #uuid "82601269-9394-5a74-98c8-230c9e6656f6" :step/math-academy-id 30437} {:db/id 17592186162839 :step/content {:db/id 17592186163218 :tutorial/content "If $(x_0,y_0)$ is any particular solution of the equation, then the set of all solutions consists of integer pairs

$$
\left(x_0 + \dfrac{b}{d}t, \: y_0 - \dfrac{a}{d}t \right), \qquad t = 0, \pm 1, \pm2, \ldots \:
$$
